title: The field and the one who knows it

verses.sa: अर्जुन उवाचप्रकृतिं पुरुषं चैव क्षेत्रं क्षेत्रज्ञमेव च । एतद्वेदितुमिच्छामि ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं च केशव ॥
verses.tr: Arjuna says: O Keshava, I wish to understand nature, the field, the knower of the field, wisdom, and what is to be known.
verses.angle: Arjuna asks about the field and the knower
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna asks Krishna to explain nature, the field, the knower of the field, wisdom, and what is to be known.

body.text: Arjuna says: O Keshava, I wish to understand nature, the field, the knower of the field, wisdom, and what is to be known. The verse pairs the field and the knower of the field, and adds wisdom and what is to be known to Arjuna's list. Arjuna asks what is to be known. Krishna answers by calling the body the field and the knower of that field the field-knower.

verses.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचइदं शरीरं कौन्तेय क्षेत्रमित्यभिधीयते । एतद्यो वेत्ति तं प्राहुः क्षेत्रज्ञ इति तद्विदः ॥
verses.tr: The body is called the field, O Arjuna. Those who know it call the knower of the field the field-knower.
verses.angle: Kshetra: the body as a field
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna begins to answer Arjuna's question with a pair of terms. Listen to how he names the body and the one who knows it.

body.text: The body is called the field, O Arjuna. Those who know it call the knower of the field the field-knower. Krishna names the body as the kshetra, the field. The one who knows this field is the kshetrajna, the knower of the field. Krishna now identifies Himself as the knower of the field in every body, Arjuna.

verses.sa: क्षेत्रज्ञं चापि मां विद्धि सर्वक्षेत्रेषु भारत । क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोर्ज्ञानं यत्तज्ज्ञानं मतं मम ॥
verses.tr: Know Me as the knower in all fields, Arjuna. In my view, true knowledge is knowing the field and the knower of the field.
verses.angle: Knowing field and knower as the real knowledge
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna shifts from the body as a field to the knower inside it. Listen to how he names the one who knows.

body.text: Know Me as the knower in all fields, Arjuna. In my view, true knowledge is knowing the field and the knower of the field. He declares that true knowledge is not one thing but a pair, knowing the field and the knower of the field, and he places himself as the knower in every field. Now hear the field itself, its nature, its changes, and the knower of the field, in brief.

verses.sa: तत्क्षेत्रं यच्च यादृक् च यद्विकारि यतश्च यत् । स च यो यत्प्रभावश्च तत्समासेन मे श्रृणु ॥
verses.tr: Listen to the field, its nature, its changes, its source, and the knower of the field, along with that knower's powers, in brief.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Listen for the word kshetra, the field, as Krishna begins to describe it and the knower who stands within it.

body.text: Listen to the field, its nature, its changes, its source, and the knower of the field, along with that knower's powers, in brief. Krishna lists four things about the field: its nature, its changes, its source, and the powers of the knower, showing that the field is a changing object. Sages and Vedic hymns have already explained this distinction between the field and the knower.

verses.sa: ऋषिभिर्बहुधा गीतं छन्दोभिर्विविधैः पृथक् । ब्रह्मसूत्रपदैश्चैव हेतुमद्भिर्विनिश्िचतैः ॥
verses.tr: This truth about the field and the knower has been sung in many ways by sages, in varied Vedic hymns, and in the reasoned, conclusive verses of the Brahma Sutras.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just told Arjuna to listen to the field and the knower. Now he names the teachers who came before.

body.text: This truth about the field and the knower has been sung in many ways by sages, in varied Vedic hymns, and in the reasoned, conclusive verses of the Brahma Sutras. The word gitam means sung, and Krishna says sages, hymns and Brahma Sutras have already sung this truth about the field. Krishna moves on to list the parts of the field, starting with the five great elements.

verses.sa: महाभूतान्यहङ्कारो बुद्धिरव्यक्तमेव च । इन्द्रियाणि दशैकं च पञ्च चेन्द्रियगोचराः ॥
verses.tr: The five great elements, ego, intellect, the unmanifest, the ten senses, the one mind, and the five sense-objects: this is the field in brief.
verses.angle: The twenty-four elements of the field
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna continues listing the parts of the field, moving from the knower to the known. Listen to the twenty-four elements.

body.text: The five great elements, ego, intellect, the unmanifest, the ten senses, the one mind, and the five sense-objects: this is the field in brief. Krishna lists the twenty-four elements, including the five great elements, the ego, the intellect, and the unmanifest, that constitute the field. Krishna then describes how desire, pain, and consciousness move through this field, bringing its changes to life.

verses.sa: इच्छा द्वेषः सुखं दुःखं सङ्घातश्चेतनाधृतिः । एतत्क्षेत्रं समासेन सविकारमुदाहृतम् ॥
verses.tr: Desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, the body, consciousness, and steadiness: this field, together with its changes, is briefly described.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has been listing the parts of the body and the mind. But what exactly counts as the field itself, and what does it include?

body.text: Desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, the body, consciousness, and steadiness: this field, together with its changes, is briefly described. Krishna lists desire and aversion right alongside pleasure and pain, showing the field is the body and the impulses that drive it. Next, Krishna continues.

verses.tr: Absence of pride, absence of pretence, nonviolence, forgiveness, simplicity, service to the teacher, purity, steadiness, and self-control.
verses.angle: Amanitvam: emptying the self of pride
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna finishes his list of what shapes the wise. The qualities are not about grand visions, but about daily conduct.

body.text: Absence of pride, absence of pretence, nonviolence, forgiveness, simplicity, service to the teacher, purity, steadiness, and self-control. The list opens with amanitvam, the absence of pride, and adamantvam, the absence of pretence. Knowledge begins not with seeing, but with emptying the self of arrogance and show. Krishna now turns to the inner eye, describing dispassion toward sense objects and the constant seeing of the fault in birth and death.

verses.tr: Dispassion toward sense objects, absence of ego, and constant seeing of the fault in birth, death, old age, and disease.
verses.angle: Freedom begins when desire stops dressing suffering as reward.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna names one inner obstacle to clear sight, and then asks the listener to notice how he describes the endless cycle of bodily decline.

body.text: Dispassion toward sense objects, absence of ego, and constant seeing of the fault in birth, death, old age, and disease. Notice how the word ahankara, ego, appears right beside the list of birth, death, old age, and disease, and how Krishna names the seeing of these faults as a repeated act. Krishna now moves to the next step, asking the listener to let go of attachment to people and places.

verses.tr: Freedom from attachment to sons, wife, home, and the like; and constant evenness of mind in desired and undesired events.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna is still describing the field of knowledge. Listen for how he names the ordinary bonds that tie a person to the world.

body.text: Freedom from attachment to sons, wife, home, and the like; and constant evenness of mind in desired and undesired events. The word anabhisvanga, no clinging, is the key. It points not to hatred of family, but to the refusal to let sons, wife, or home hold the mind captive. Next, Krishna continues.

verses.tr: Undivided devotion to me, a love that does not waver, delight in solitude, and no attraction to crowds.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna continues his list of what it means to know the field and the knower of the field.

body.text: Undivided devotion to me, a love that does not waver, delight in solitude, and no attraction to crowds. Unwavering devotion to Krishna, a taste for solitude, and no appetite for crowds go on his list of knowledge. Krishna then tells us that seeing this supreme reality is the mark of true understanding, and anything else is ignorance.

verses.tr: Constant awareness of the inner reality, and seeing the supreme reality as the meaning of true understanding, this is called knowledge; whatever is contrary to this is ignorance.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just listed the qualities of a true student. What exactly is the goal of all this discipline? Listen for the final definition.

body.text: Constant awareness of the inner reality, and seeing the supreme reality as the meaning of true understanding, this is called knowledge; whatever is contrary to this is ignorance. Krishna ends the list by saying knowledge is steady awareness of the inner reality and seeing the supreme reality everywhere; anything else is ignorance. Krishna now begins to tell what is to be known: the beginningless supreme reality beyond existence and nonexistence.

verses.sa: ज्ञेयं यत्तत्प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञात्वाऽमृतमश्नुते । अनादिमत्परं ब्रह्म न सत्तन्नासदुच्यते ॥
verses.tr: I will now tell you what is to be known. Knowing it, one attains freedom. It is beginningless supreme reality, beyond existence and nonexistence.
verses.angle: Sat and asat cannot describe the supreme
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna now moves from the student to the knowledge itself, pointing to the beginningless reality that frees the knower.

body.text: I will now tell you what is to be known. Knowing it, one attains freedom. It is beginningless supreme reality, beyond existence and nonexistence. The verse denies both terms, calling the supreme reality neither sat, existent, nor asat, nonexistent. It is the truth that stands beyond these two opposites. Krishna then describes how this reality pervades the world, having hands and feet everywhere.

verses.sa: सर्वतः पाणिपादं तत्सर्वतोऽक्षिशिरोमुखम् । सर्वतः श्रुतिमल्लोके सर्वमावृत्य तिष्ठति ॥
verses.tr: The supreme reality has hands and feet everywhere, eyes, heads, and faces everywhere, and ears everywhere. It pervades all things and stands within all things.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Listen closely to the body Krishna gives to the supreme reality: it has hands, feet, eyes, and ears everywhere.

body.text: The supreme reality has hands and feet everywhere, eyes, heads, and faces everywhere, and ears everywhere. It pervades all things and stands within all things. Notice the word Sarvatah, everywhere. It appears three times, telling you that there is no place, no direction, and no being outside of this reality. Krishna then tells you that this same reality has no senses, yet it lights up every sense object.

verses.sa: सर्वेन्द्रियगुणाभासं सर्वेन्द्रियविवर्जितम् । असक्तं सर्वभृच्चैव निर्गुणं गुणभोक्तृ च ॥
verses.tr: The supreme reality has no senses, yet illumines every sense-object. It is detached, supports all beings, beyond the three qualities, and yet experiences the qualities.
verses.angle: Devoid of senses, yet lighting all sense-objects
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just described Brahman as having hands, feet, and eyes everywhere. Now He turns to a deeper mystery, speaking to Arjuna about a reality that is both here and beyond.

body.text: The supreme reality has no senses, yet illumines every sense-object. It is detached, supports all beings, beyond the three qualities, and yet experiences the qualities. Notice how Krishna speaks of a reality that is devoid of all senses, yet shines through every object the senses touch, and is without qualities, yet the enjoyer of all qualities. Krishna then explains that this subtle reality is both near and far, inside and outside all beings.
